prompt: What security measures does NIS2 Article 21 actually require us to implement?
assertions: Lists the all-hazards, 10-measure minimum set — policies on risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity/backup/DR/crisis management, supply chain security, secure development/vulnerability handling, effectiveness testing, cyber hygiene/training, cryptography policies, HR/access control/asset management, and MFA/secured communications
Emphasises supply chain security including direct supplier relationships as an explicit measure
Notes proportionality: measures appropriate to the risks, entity size, and societal impact
Mentions the effectiveness-assessment obligation (policies and procedures to assess whether measures work)
Frames ISO 27001 correctly if raised: strong implementation vehicle but not a safe harbor (registration, reporting timelines, governance duties sit outside certification)
